name: The Portal (Downtown Rail Extension)
aliases: Transbay Downtown Rail Extension Project, Phase 2
acresNote: A rail line, not a site: a 1.3-mile tunnel from Fourth and King to the Salesforce Transit Center, 2.2 miles of total construction including trackwork in Caltrain's Fourth and King railyard (TJPA, 2026). No official footprint acreage was found. The 2018 Final SEIS/EIR gave longer lengths (2.7 miles with a turnback track at Mariposa Street, 2 miles without it), which have since been superseded. Approximate center is the midpoint of the tunnel line in the California High-Speed Rail Authority's statewide alignment layer (section 'DTX').

program.notes: A transit project, so the building program fields do not apply. Scope: a mostly underground rail extension along Townsend and Second Streets, built by cut-and-cover and mined tunneling. It includes a new underground Fourth and Townsend Street Station (two tracks, a center platform and two side platforms, serving Caltrain), the fit-out of the existing two-level train box under the Salesforce Transit Center (six tracks and three center platforms for Caltrain and high-speed rail), ventilation and emergency exit structures, and trackwork in Caltrain's Fourth and King railyard. The 2026 scope changes removed the high-speed rail platforms at Fourth and Townsend, the train box extension and the intercity bus facility. They also shortened the tunnel stub box by about 750 feet. Project budget: $8.255 billion in year-of-expenditure dollars (2023 estimate, including the completed train box, contingency and financing). The 2025 updated estimate is about $7.572 billion, and TJPA holds the difference as unallocated contingency. FTA's Capital Investment Grant share is $3.38 billion. TJPA's July 2026 funding plan lists $1,304 million committed from non-CIG sources, $1,303 million in planned state funds, $265 million in other planned sources and $729 million already invested in the train box, which leaves a $587 million gap. TJPA forecasts over 125,000 average daily riders.

developer: Transbay Joint Powers Authority (TJPA), lead agency
publicPartners: Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board (Caltrain), primary rail operator
San Francisco County Transportation Authority (Prop K and Prop L sales tax)
City and County of San Francisco
Federal Transit Administration (Capital Investment Grants, New Starts)
stageNote: Environmentally cleared and in the Engineering phase of FTA's Capital Investment Grants program since May 2024, but not yet under construction or fully funded. Design is at 30% for the tunnel and stations and 60% for the early works. Right-of-way appraisals are under way, and proposals for the civil and tunnel progressive design-build contract are due Oct 9, 2026. The Full Funding Grant Agreement is targeted for July 2027. TJPA says utility relocation construction will start in 2028 and forecasts that the line will be ready for service on Nov 17, 2036.

timeline.event: San Francisco voters pass Proposition H, calling for Caltrain to be extended into downtown.
The federal Record of Decision completes environmental review of the Transbay Program, including the downtown extension.
The Salesforce Transit Center opens (Transbay Program Phase 1), with an empty two-level train box built for the future rail extension.
TJPA certifies the Final Supplemental EIS/EIR for refinements to the Transbay Program, including the downtown extension.
FTA issues an Amended Record of Decision for the Supplemental EIS/EIR.
Six agencies agree to the San Francisco Peninsula Rail Program MOU to advance the project together.
The project enters the Project Development phase of FTA's Capital Investment Grants program.
TJPA's Board adopts the first CEQA addendum (design refinements); FTA concurs with the matching NEPA re-evaluation on June 9, 2023.
FTA approves entry into the New Starts Engineering phase and sets the federal grant share at $3.38 billion.
The six partner agencies execute The Portal Project Implementation MOU.
TJPA's Board receives an updated cost estimate of $7.57 billion; the $8.255 billion budget is kept.
TJPA issues the request for proposals for the civil and tunnel progressive design-build contract.
TJPA's Board adopts the second CEQA addendum (removing the intercity bus facility, the train box extension and the high-speed rail platforms at Fourth and Townsend; acquiring 171 Second Street).
TJPA applies for $750 million from the state's Transit and Intercity Rail Capital Program (Cycle 8).
FTA concurs with the NEPA re-evaluation of the 2026 scope changes, finding no new significant impacts.
The Governor signs AB 2308, extending Transbay tax increment by 25 years beyond 2050 to help fund the project.

nextMilestone: Civil and tunnel design-build proposals are due Oct 9, 2026, with the highest-scoring proposer to be named Nov 6, 2026 and the contract awarded Feb 11, 2027. The state's TIRCP Cycle 8 awards are expected in October 2026. The Full Funding Grant Agreement is targeted for July 2027.
summary: A rail tunnel to bring Caltrain, and later high-speed rail, from the Fourth and King terminus about 1.3 miles into the Salesforce Transit Center, whose two-level underground train box was built for it and has stood empty since 2018. It adds an underground station at Fourth and Townsend. The $8.3 billion project is environmentally cleared and in federal engineering review, with a $3.38 billion federal grant in sight. It still needs the rest of its local and state funding, and TJPA forecasts service in late 2036.
massingNotes: Draw as a line with two station points, not as buildings, and label it 'Approximate alignment'. Best official geometry: (1) The 2018 Final SEIS/EIR Volume 1 (tjpa.org), Figure 2-2 'Approved Transbay Program Phase 2 - DTX Alignment and Construction' (PDF p. 91), Figure 2-6 'Proposed Project Components' (PDF p. 105), Figure 2-9a Fourth and Townsend station plan and profile (PDF p. 108) and Figure 2-21 construction methods by location (PDF p. 136). (2) Figure 1 'The Portal Alignment and Major Components' in TJPA's September 2026 Monthly Status Report (p. 4), which reflects the 2026 scope. (3) The California High-Speed Rail Authority's ArcGIS layers have a 'DTX (Downtown Extension)' polyline of about 1.33 miles (services3.arcgis.com/rGGp0aiv6Rf11t2H, HSR_Statewide_Alignment layer 1 and Alignment_Hybrid_Feb_8_2024 layer 4). Their terms say the data 'are not to be redistributed without the express approval' of the Authority, so use them only to check a trace unless permission is granted. No TJPA or DataSF GIS layer was found. Stations: the Salesforce Transit Center train box, under the block between Beale and Second Streets at Mission and Fremont; Fourth and Townsend under Townsend Street between Fourth and Fifth Streets. The 2026 changes shortened the tunnel stub box by about 750 feet, so the 2018 figures overstate the west end.
verify: the opening date: TJPA's July 2025 fact sheet and project page say 2035 'funding dependent'; the Sept 2026 status report forecasts ready-for-service on Nov 17, 2036; FTA's oversight consultant's July 2026 report lists a target of July 16, 2036 and a risk-based FFGA date of June 27, 2035
the civil and tunnel proposal due date: the Sept 2026 status report says Oct 9, 2026 in its text (p. 3) and Sept 25, 2026 in its six-month lookahead (p. 8)
the outcome of TIRCP Cycle 8 (TJPA applied for $750 million; awards delayed to October 2026)

the funding gap, which depends on how the sources are counted: $2,131 million (TJPA fact sheet, July 2025), about $2.2 billion (SFCTA memo, Jan 2026), $587 million 'to be planned' after $1,303 million of planned state funds (TJPA funding plan, July 2026)

CHSRA's $550 million commitment: the September 2026 report says TJPA must 'recommence conversations' with CHSRA because of its new business plan, while the 2026 Business Plan says the Authority 'remains committed to securing at least $550 million'
the Oct 8, 2026 TJPA Board item 'The Portal Update and Monthly Status Report for September 2026', and whether the Board took any new actions
the date of the second NEPA re-evaluation request: TJPA's report says Aug 5, 2026 and FTA's letter says the package is dated Aug 4, 2026
a drawable alignment: trace from the SEIS/EIR figures, or get CHSRA's permission to use its DTX polyline
